rostow-stages.def: A model by W. W. Rostow (1960) that says countries develop through five stages: traditional society, preconditions for take-off, take-off, drive to maturity and high mass consumption.

world-system-theory.def: Immanuel Wallerstein's model of one connected world economy in which countries play core, semiperiphery or periphery roles, and can move between them.

dependency-theory.def: A theory that says poorer countries stay poor because of their dependence on richer ones, built through colonial rule and trade in raw materials for factory goods.
